draft.title: Protecting investors
card: Investing carries risk, and investors often rely on advice from others. Laws and regulators exist to protect people from unfair or dishonest treatment.
ASIC
the Australian Securities and Investments Commission. It regulates financial markets and the businesses that give financial advice, and it can act against those that break the rules.
Licensing
a person or business that gives financial advice in Australia must hold a licence. This lets clients check that an adviser is authorised to give advice.
Best interests
licensed advisers must act in their clients' best interests. They must put the client's needs ahead of their own, such as the commission they might earn.
draft.remember: ASIC regulates markets and advisers. Advisers must be licensed and put clients' interests first.

a.q: Which of these is a role of ASIC?
opts: Regulating financial advisers and markets
Setting the interest rate on bank deposits
Guaranteeing that shares will rise in value
Choosing which investments clients should buy
a.why: ASIC regulates financial markets and the businesses that give advice. It does not set deposit rates, promise returns or pick investments for clients. Investments can still lose value even when markets are well regulated.
a.clue: Think of ASIC as a referee, not a player.

b.q: Dan's adviser in Orange recommends a managed fund because it pays the adviser a high commission, even though a cheaper fund suits Dan better. Which rule has the adviser most clearly broken?
opts: Acting in the client's best interests
Holding a licence to give advice
Regulating the financial market
Reporting to ASIC each year
b.why: Advisers must put the client's needs ahead of their own, including any commission. Choosing a fund for the commission breaks this duty. Holding a licence is a different rule, and the case does not say the adviser lacked one.
b.clue: Whose needs came first in the adviser's choice?

b.best: Acting in the client's best interests

problems.detail: 'A person or business that gives financial advice in Australia must hold a licence' is not quite accurate. The business needs an Australian financial services licence. An individual adviser usually works as an authorised representative of a licensee and is listed on the Financial Advisers Register, and does not hold a licence of their own. Consider wording such as 'must be licensed or authorised by a licensed business'.

check.summary: Both questions are sound and the explanations match the card. One small fact issue: the card says every individual adviser must hold a licence, but individual advisers usually act under a licensed business's licence.

ASIC
the Australian Securities and Investments Commission. It regulates financial markets and the businesses that give financial advice, and it can act against those that break the rules.
Licensing
a business that gives financial advice must hold a licence. Each adviser must be licensed or authorised by a licensed business, and clients can check advisers on a public register kept by ASIC.
Best interests
advisers must act in their clients' best interests. They must put the client's needs ahead of their own, such as the commission they might earn.
